title: New York City Transit Authority: Objects

description.main: A photographic catalogue of more than 400 New York City Transit Authority objects from the collection of Brian Kelley.
description.extended:
A photographic catalogue of New York City Transit Authority ephemera from the collection of the photographer Brian Kelley, with more than 400 objects dating back to the 1850s.

Kelley began in 2011 by photographing grids of used MetroCards in his Brooklyn studio, then widened the search to patches, matchbooks, tokens, timetables, pins and signs. By 2017 his collection held more than 2,000 items. The objects appear in no fixed order, and Eric Greene's introduction describes the project as a photography experiment that grew into an archive. Jesse Reed and Hamish Smyth edited the book.

Standards Manual, a Brooklyn publisher, issued the 356-page book in 2017 as a case-bound 10 by 10 inch volume with a silkscreened cover and Italian cloth, printed in Italy. Kelley opened Tumblr and Instagram accounts for the project in 2014. All objects shown are reproduced with the permission of the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
